sourceRefs.locator: Chapters X–XI. Witmar as a witness, loss of the books en route, permission to preach, captive Christians, Herigar and his church. The narrative is used for the visit. Modern site identification follows the Swedish History Museum.
Opening paragraphs. Rimbert wrote about 865–875. The museum dates Ansgar and Witmar’s first journey to 830 and distinguishes it from Ansgar’s later visit.
Handelsplatsen Birka. Björkö stood at a Baltic inlet at the time of the trading settlement. The present lake resulted from land uplift. Also explains the deposits called Svarta jorden.
Geographical data, component 555-001, Birka on Björkö (not 555-002, Hovgården). A rounded site point is shared by the harbour, burial and hoard stations.
Object 106842_HST, accession 34000, Bj 515. Find context, excavator, 1877, silver and glass. The 2021 exhibition label gives the proposed reading of the Arabic inscription.

Scanning 37, pp. 131–137. Materials, p. 132 and supplementary fig. S1, for burial layout, oval brooches, clothes, position and approximate date. Results and figs. 1–3 for filing marks and composition. Discussion accompanying fig. 4 for the favoured dedication and the conditional reading “God willing” if a missing stroke is supplied.
Media ID ba934209-835b-4b3c-ab7a-73126a4375a9, direct association with object 106842_HST, named photographer and CC BY 4.0 licence.

Section Rūs, paragraphs 74–78 and pp. 27–29. Merchants at the Itil, houses on the bank, enslaved women, sable pelts, offerings and hoped-for buyer. The translation indicates where Yāqūt’s quotations parallel the Mashhad recension.
The Journey of Ibn Fadlan, 921–922, map. Pages 25–26, The reading of the caliph’s letter, for the embassy’s arrival in May 922. The market on the Volga, p. 40.
Introduction and annotated translation of the Rūsiyyah passage. The identification of the group seen by the envoy allows more than one interpretation.
Component 981-001, N54°58′44″ E49°03′23″. A regional point on the middle Volga. The archaeological site gives geographic orientation only.

Transactions 23, p. 60, description of the 1872 Birka hoard and the al-Maṣṣīṣa issue dated 963/64 by the author. Also the Volga Bulgar attributions. Pages 73–75 discuss the Byzantine frontier, the capture of al-Maṣṣīṣa in 965, service and payment as possible contexts.

Adelsö, no. 16B, SHM/KMK 5208:3. Wärner found the dish on 18 September 1872. Quotes Stolpe’s excavation notes with depth and counts of whole and broken coins. Lists al-Masisah, 963–967, and a second broadly dated late issue.
Report on the silver hoard, especially the inventory and discussion of Tornberg’s readings. Compares the readings 963 and 967 and distinguishes minting from the unknown date of burial.

Toponym entry 1443. Modern name Yakapınar (Misis), Barrington Atlas 67 B3, Pleiades 658538 and discussion of the settlement by the Pyramos. The city marks the district of production. The position of the coin workshop is unknown.

Opening description of the 1872 iron dish and uncertainty of its precise findspot. Paragraph on the larger 1991 find with seven weights. Sections on coin pendants and the two wave lines under the ship on the Hedeby coin from grave Bj 526.

labels.de: Ein Ring und ein Dirham in Birka
labels.en: A ring and a dirham at Birka

labels.de: um 830 · Ansgar und Witmar erreichen den Hafen
labels.en: around 830 · Ansgar and Witmar reach the harbour

summary.de: Rimbert schildert die Ankunft der beiden Mönche, die Gefangenen und den Ortsvorsteher Hergeir. Der Punkt bezeichnet die Handelsstadt auf Björkö.
summary.en: Rimbert recounts the monks’ arrival and describes captives and the town’s reeve, Hergeir. The point marks the trading settlement on Björkö.

labels.de: 9. Jahrhundert, wohl um 850 · Ein Ring kommt in Grab Bj 515
labels.en: ninth century, probably around 850 · A ring is placed in grave Bj 515

summary.de: Stolpes Grabungsdokumentation verzeichnet den Ring neben einer Schere. Die Gewandspangen stützen eine Datierung um die Mitte des 9. Jahrhunderts. Die Karte zeigt Birka, das Grab lag nördlich der Befestigung.
summary.en: Stolpe’s excavation record places the ring beside a pair of scissors. The brooch types suggest a date around the middle of the ninth century. The map marks Birka. The grave lay north of its fortress.

labels.de: 922 · Ibn Faḍlān begegnet den Rūs an der Wolga
labels.en: 922 · Ibn Faḍlān meets the Rūs on the Volga

summary.de: Der Gesandte beschreibt Verkäufer und versklavte Frauen an einem Ufer der mittleren Wolga. Der Punkt bei Bolgar zeigt die Region. Der genaue Anlegeplatz ist unbekannt.
summary.en: The envoy describes sellers and enslaved women on the middle Volga. The point at Bolgar represents the region. The exact landing is unknown.

labels.de: 963–967 · Ein Dirham aus der Münzstadt al-Maṣṣīṣa
labels.en: 963–967 · A dirham from the mint town of al-Maṣṣīṣa

summary.de: Der Fundkatalog gibt für die hamdanidische Prägung in al-Maṣṣīṣa 963–967 an. Androshchuk liest 963/64. Der Punkt bezeichnet die Stadt Mopsuestia, in der der Dirham entstand.
summary.en: The hoard catalogue gives the Hamdanid issue from al-Maṣṣīṣa a range of 963–967. Androshchuk reads 963/64. The point marks the town of Mopsuestia where the coin was struck.

labels.de: 1872 · Wärner entdeckt den Teller mit dem Silber
labels.en: 1872 · Wärner uncovers the silver on its dish

summary.de: Am 18. September 1872 fand ein Arbeiter namens Wärner einen Teller voller Silber im einstigen Siedlungsgebiet von Birka. Das Fundjahr ist gesichert. Die genaue Fundstelle und das Jahr der Niederlegung sind unbekannt.
summary.en: On 18 September 1872 a workman named Wärner found a dishful of silver in the former settlement at Birka. The year of discovery is secure. The precise findspot and year of burial are unknown.

summary.de: Ein Ring mit arabischer Inschrift lag in einem Grab bei Birka. Ein Dirham aus derselben Siedlung führt nach Kilikien. An der Wolga beschreibt Ibn Faḍlān die Geschäfte der Rūs und die Menschen, die sie zum Verkauf brachten.
summary.en: A ring with Arabic writing lay in a grave at Birka. A dirham from the settlement can be traced to Cilicia. On the Volga, Ibn Faḍlān describes the business done by Rūs traders, including the people they brought for sale.

sourceRefs.locator: U841.4 and U842.2, especially the twice-occurring longport and the phrase for the continuing presence at Duiblinn. Printed Irish text p. 300.

U841.4 and U842.2, two camps and continued presence; U870.6, four months at Ail Cluaithe; U871.2, Áth Cliath, the leaders, 200 ships and the three groups brought back as captives; U902.2 and U917.4, the defenders driven out and Sitriuc’s entry. U980.1 and U983.2, the battle of Tara and later coalitions.

T979.2, capture of Domnall Claen; T980.3–4, Tara and the subsequent siege, agreed terms, named hostage, three days and nights, and the biblical simile (folio 15a2, printed pp. 341–342). T983.1 gives the later opposing coalitions.

Section 2.1.3, “Viking and Norman Dublin”, printed p. 9, on the Liffey crossing and the pool of the Poddle. The existing point represents the Dublin area rather than a shipyard, landing or mint building.
“Dublin Your Knowledge”, pp. 86–88, map of the sites by the former black pool, proposed longphort on its south bank and explicit discussion of the debated location.
Section 2.1.1–2.1.2, printed pp. 3–4. The two placenames, proposed camp by the pool, events of 902 and 917 and changing focus around the Liffey shore at Fishamble Street and Wood Quay.

SC1365, “Summary” and “Location”; twin summits, 1974–75 excavation, fifth trench on the eastern side, bedding trench, vitrified stone and three radiocarbon determinations in the sixth to ninth centuries. Site coordinates WGS84, 55.936756 N, 4.563298 W.
“Under siege”, identification of the 870 siege of the Rock, the Dublin leaders Olaf and Ivar, and forced removals following the four-month siege.

EMAP Report 7.1, printed pp. 53–55, discussion of captive-taking, trade in enslaved people at Dublin, possibilities of domestic enslavement or onward sale, and the limits of the evidence for different destinations.

Chapter 2, pp. 7–13, property boundaries, plot and house layouts, fifteen building levels; chapter 4, p. 38, Level 4, FS 20 (Plot 2, amber) and FS 18 (Plot 5, writing tablet, carved head, coin of Eadred); p. 82 for Level 4 as mid-tenth century. Fig. 9, p. 36, grid on Plot 3, used to orient the Fishamble Street excavation area.
Excavations 1976:047, habitation area inside the banks, amber fragments and unfinished beads and pendants. These finds illustrate working at Fishamble Street more generally.

Collection overview, paragraphs on wooden pathways and property boundaries, reused ship timbers in dock walls, drains and paths; the Fishamble Street amber worker’s floor with several hundred flakes and splinters.

British Numismatic Journal 78, p. 116 table 1 and pp. 122–124. First Irish issues in the 990s and their English prototypes; p. 124 and notes 65–68 distinguish English dies used in Dublin and Hiberno-Scandinavian-style dies at York.
“Viking coinage” and preceding paragraph. The museum puts the earliest Dublin pennies under Sihtric at around 997 or 998; English and other coins were circulating earlier.

PAS FindID 147193, HESH-E20370, image 203021. The PAS description, photograph and scale identify the Long Cross type modelled on Æthelred II, moneyer Faeremin, Dublin mint and Shropshire findspot. Record date field 1000–1010; image description, author and CC BY-SA 4.0 credit on the file page.
The rulers of Dublin and mid-tenth-century York, chronology; Mark Blackburn’s chapter on the coinage, pp. 335–336, fig. 82.2, raven issue of Óláfr/Amlaíb Guthfrithsson in 939–941.

Printed pp. 183–186, keelson sample D2-4 and its final spring ring; pp. 187–189, “Parallels in Irish and English ship-finds”, esp. fig. 55 (Fishamble Street stems T357/T364 and corresponding elements of Skuldelev 2) and text on parallels in Danish-built vessels.
Opening account, dating the build to around 1042 in the vicinity of Dublin through the oak tree rings.

labels.en: 841 · The annals record a ship camp

summary.de: Die Annalen von Ulster nennen ein Schiffslager bei Duiblinn und Überfälle auf das Umland. Der Punkt verortet die Gegend des heutigen Dublin. Die genaue Lage des Lagers ist umstritten.
summary.en: The Annals of Ulster record a ship camp at Duiblinn and raids into neighbouring lands. The point marks the Dublin area. The precise site of the camp is debated.

summary.de: Amlaíb und Ímar nahmen die Festung nach einer viermonatigen Belagerung ein. Der Felsen ist archäologisch identifiziert. Die Brandspuren lassen sich nur allgemein ins frühe Mittelalter datieren.
summary.en: Amlaíb and Ímar took the stronghold after a four-month siege. Excavations locate the early defences on Dumbarton Rock. The evidence of burning has only a broad early medieval date.

summary.de: Die Annalen melden, dass Amlaíb und Ímar mit Gefangenen nach Áth Cliath kamen. Sie zählen Schiffe und nennen Gruppen von Verschleppten. Was aus den einzelnen Menschen wurde, steht dort nicht.
summary.en: The annals say that Amlaíb and Ímar brought captives to Áth Cliath. They count ships and name groups of people who were taken. Individual fates go unrecorded.

labels.de: Mitte des 10. Jahrhunderts · Eine Werkstatt in der Fishamble Street
labels.en: mid-tenth century · A workshop on Fishamble Street

summary.de: Bernsteinreste deuten auf eine Werkstatt in Haus FS 20 auf Grundstück 2. Eine Münze hilft bei der Datierung der vierten Bauphase um die Mitte des zehnten Jahrhunderts. Die Karte zeigt das Grabungsareal.
summary.en: Amber debris suggests a workshop in house FS 20 on Plot 2. A coin helps date the fourth building phase to around the middle of the tenth century. The map marks the excavation area.

summary.de: Die Annalen von Tigernach nennen den König von Leinster unter den Geiseln, die nach der Belagerung Dublins durch Máel Sechnaill und Eochaid freikamen. Der Bericht zählt auch die ausgehandelten Bedingungen auf.
summary.en: The Annals of Tigernach name the king of Leinster among the hostages released after Máel Sechnaill and Eochaid besieged Dublin. The entry also lists the terms the victors obtained.

labels.de: um 1000–1010 · Ein Penny des Münzmeisters Faeremin
labels.en: c. 1000–1010 · A penny of the moneyer Faeremin

summary.de: Der in Shropshire gefundene Penny HESH-E20370 wird dem Dubliner Münzmeister Faeremin zugeschrieben und in die Jahre um 1000–1010 eingeordnet. Die Karte zeigt den Prägeort Dublin, der genaue Werkstattstandort ist unbekannt.
summary.en: Penny HESH-E20370, found in Shropshire, is attributed to the Dublin moneyer Faeremin and dated to about 1000–1010. The map marks the mint town. The location of the workshop is unknown.

labels.de: 1042 · Die Eiche für die Maststütze von Skuldelev 2
labels.en: 1042 · The oak for the keelson of Skuldelev 2

summary.de: Die Eiche für die Maststütze fiel im Mai oder Juni 1042. Der Bau des Langschiffs wird im Raum Dublin vermutet. Zwei in der Stadt ausgegrabene Stevenstücke zeigen vergleichbare Arbeit an anderen Schiffen.
summary.en: The oak for the keelson was felled in May or June 1042. The longship was probably built in the Dublin region. Two stem timbers excavated in the town show comparable work on other vessels.

summary.de: Gefangene erreichen 871 die Liffey. Bernsteinsplitter verraten den Arbeitsplatz eines Menschen in der Fishamble Street, ein Silberpenny den Namen des Münzmeisters Faeremin.
summary.en: Captives reach the Liffey in 871. Chips of amber locate a workshop on Fishamble Street, and a silver penny preserves the name of Faeremin, a Dublin moneyer.

sourceRefs.locator: The exhibition at Aðalstræti 16, in the original location of the tenth-century hall. The listing distinguishes the earlier wall fragment. Map point at 64.14749° N, 21.94251° W locates the exhibition on the archaeological site.

FS243-00162, Summary, the paved structure at the eastern doorway. Appendix 4, Karen B. Milek, sections on preservation of occupation deposits and the central hearth. Floor deposits were sealed by collapsed turf roofing.

NORSEC 2, pp. 1–4 and Figs. 5–7. Square-metre sampling, sieving heavy fraction through 1 mm mesh, about 3% identifiable, taxa and calcination. Authors interpret spatial distributions as possible hearth raking and trampling near walls and benches.

Chapter 7, pp. 102–108, Figs. 7.2–4 and Table 7.1. Hearth 4A76P west of the brook, 15 grey-green chert flakes one metre west of the fire, the nail one metre southeast. With 1950 as BP reference, the reported two-sigma charcoal ranges are AD 900–910 and 960–1040 for Beta-252632 and AD 990–1150 for Beta-252633. The map uses their outer envelope; occupation was episodic. pp. 115–116 and Tables 7.5–6 describe birds on the other, upper terrace.

Arctic Anthropology 49(1), pp. 68–87, DOI 10.1353/arc.2012.0015. Abstract and Table 1 discuss the site in relation to Beothuk ancestors, the charcoal determinations for hearth 4A76P2 and seasonal harvesting of birds.

“Discovery of the Site and Initial Excavations (1960–1968)”. Turf construction in eight buildings, bronze ring-headed pin in a cooking pit, stone lamp and spindle whorl in another building, ship nails and iron slag.
Collection entry “Bog Iron Nail, L’Anse aux Meadows, Newfoundland”. Slag and iron from the excavated nail support smelting of local bog ore. The four nails illustrated on that page are reproductions.
Appendix 1, pp. 30–31, manuscript witnesses AM 544 4to and GKS 1005 fol., and “B. Differences”: one planned expedition in Eiríks saga rauða and four in Grœnlendinga saga.

Meddelelser om Grønland, Man & Society 28, abstract and farm economy synthesis. Three phases, dental ages of dairy cattle, change from harbour to harp seal, 166 fish bones found exclusively in sieved samples; char, cod and capelin. The assemblage is not a quantitative measure of the diet.

Antiquity 83, pp. 430–444. Fig. 1 and site introduction describe alluvial cover. Sampling and Replication, especially p. 439, report cattle, sheep and goat DNA in open-field core samples dated AD 1215–1285 and 1305–1365. The station follows the latter sediment sample.
Site description pp. 46–47 and Figs. 11–12. Farm at 64°06′ N, 50°05′ W in the valley at the head of Ameralla fjord. Coordinate refers to the archaeological locality, not to the soil core.

Collection no. DMR-216754, filename 003_33868.tif. Field photograph taken during the six excavation seasons of 1992–1997. Photographer and CC BY-SA 4.0 are identified in the record. The farm is mapped from the excavation research.

Introductory chronology, “Geographical areas of the Norse settlements and settlement pattern” and “Natural resources”. The written sources place one migration from Iceland to Southwest Greenland under Erik the Red around 985. The Western Settlement was in the Nuuk region; archaeological and radiocarbon evidence in the Eastern Settlement reaches at least the mid-fifteenth century.

Printed pp. 146, 148–149 and 152–153. P. 146 describes the transmitted attestations of 1409, 1414 and 1424. Document 49 gives the three Sunday banns, local and foreign witnesses, and the two clerics’ seals. Document 52 names the four men who attended in 1408 and attested in Iceland in 1414. Facsimile of the edition with facing original text and Danish translation.

“Kirkens vinduer” on the round arched east window and other flat lintels; “Brylluppet i Hvalseyfjordens kirke” on the September 1408 wedding, the document at Garðar in 1409 and the journey back to Iceland.
Collection item DMR-217737, ruin 1, group Ø83, NKAH 4427 (Hvalsey church). Location field 60.82883° N, 45.78261° W. Modern survey photograph dated 1935.

Nature 601, pp. 388–391. Three worked pieces of wood, the metal-tool cuts and Norse depositional context, Table 1 and Fig. 2 on the radiocarbon signal and counting rings to the surviving outside edge. Published online in 2021.
First two paragraphs. Archaeological evidence of Indigenous use over six millennia and Dorset camps on the south shore more than two centuries before the Norse.
Official national historic site point ACPWM, 51.5952777 N, 55.5330555 W; used for the site, not individual wood samples.

labels.en: Farms and hearths on the North Atlantic
10th century · The hearth in the longhouse

summary.de: Im Fußboden einer Halle aus dem 10. Jahrhundert blieben winzige verbrannte Knochen erhalten. Der Punkt zeigt den erhaltenen Befund in der Aðalstræti.
summary.en: Tiny pieces of burnt bone survived in the floor of a tenth-century hall. The point marks the preserved excavation on Aðalstræti.

labels.de: etwa 900–1150 · Eine indigene Feuerstelle am Bach
labels.en: roughly 900–1150 · An Indigenous hearth by the brook

summary.de: 15 Hornsteinabschläge lagen westlich der Feuerstelle. Die Karte zeigt den Fundortkomplex und die äußeren Grenzen der beiden Holzkohledatierungen. Ob die Feuerstelle und die nordischen Häuser gleichzeitig genutzt wurden, bleibt offen.
summary.en: Fifteen chert flakes lay west of the hearth. The point locates the archaeological site. The window covers the outer limits of two charcoal dates; whether the hearth and the Norse buildings were used at the same time remains open.

summary.de: Die drei Hölzer datieren Arbeiten auf 1021. Nägel, Schlacke und Spinnwirtel bezeugen weitere Tätigkeiten im Lager, deren genaues Jahr offenbleibt.
summary.en: Three timbers date work at the camp to 1021. Nails, slag and a spindle whorl attest other activities there whose precise year is unknown.

labels.de: 1305–1365 · Vieh auf dem Hof unter dem Sand
labels.en: 1305–1365 · Livestock at the Farm Beneath the Sand

summary.de: Eine Bodenschicht im Feld barg Erbmaterial von Rindern, Schafen und Ziegen. Das Zeitfenster gehört zur jüngeren der zwei unabhängig geprüften Proben. Der Punkt markiert den Hof in der Westsiedlung.
summary.en: Soil from the field contained DNA of cattle, sheep and goats. The window dates the younger of two independently tested samples. The point marks the farm in the Western Settlement.

labels.de: 1408 · Die Hochzeit von Sigríður und Þorsteinn

summary.de: Im September 1408 heirateten Sigríður Björnsdóttir und Þorsteinn Ólafsson in der Kirche von Hvalsey. Die Bestätigung der Geistlichen in Garðar und spätere Zeugenaussagen in Island betreffen dieselbe Ehe.
summary.en: In September 1408 Sigríður Björnsdóttir and Þorsteinn Ólafsson married in Hvalsey church. The Garðar clerics’ declaration and later testimony in Iceland concern the same marriage.

summary.de: Ein Langhausboden in Reykjavík, eine indigene Feuerstelle und ein Spinnwirtel in Neufundland erzählen von der Arbeit am Atlantik. In Grönland führen Tierknochen auf einen Bauernhof und Zeugenaussagen zu einer Hochzeit von 1408.
summary.en: A Reykjavík house floor, an Indigenous hearth and a spindle whorl in Newfoundland preserve traces of work around the Atlantic. In Greenland, animal bones lead to an inland farm and witnesses recall a wedding in 1408.

sourceRefs.locator: Hull and rowing holes, the ship built in 820, burial of two women in 834 and the uncertainty over their identities and status.

“The Jelling Stone”, translated inscription and photographs. The museum dates the raising to c. 965. Harald’s parents and claims about Denmark, Norway and Christianity, earlier Christian objects and Harald Klak’s baptism at Mainz in 826.

“Gorm the Old authored Denmark’s name certificate” and “Two monuments from Danish history”. Gorm’s commissioning formula, the museum’s rendering of Thyra’s epithet, c. 950, and the photograph “The small Jelling stone” by Roberto Fortuna, CC BY-SA 2.0.
Geographical data table, property 697bis, N55° 45′ 23″ E9° 25′ 12″.

Antiquity 97, 1262–1278. Table 1, introduction on the north mound, “Ravnunge-Tue and the Jelling stones”, figures 9–10, “Sources of error” and conclusion. Læborg’s signed dedication and proposed attribution of Jelling 2, weathering at Jelling 1, variants of Thyra’s epithet, and limits of the proposed reburial. The authors give 959/60 for wood from the chamber.

Abstract of chapter 12 in Jelling – Monuments and Landscape, pp. 313–332. The smaller stone is no longer in its original position. Excavation during protection works in 2011 re-examined the central area and the position of the larger stone.

Danish Journal of Archaeology 3(2), pp. 168–170, tables 1–2 and discussion immediately after table 2. Mid-tenth century up to c. 960 for Jelling 1. The chamber wood is reported as 958/59. Historical dating proposals for Jelling 2 differ.

Figures 2–6 and English summary under “Stone for his parents” and “Small silver cup”. Vertical and horizontal writing, reliefs, purple silk, and the 4.3 cm silver cup with gilding and entwined animals from the north mound.
Object DO-1525. Description of the west-facing section and view of the burial chamber (Tabula I, 1823); Placering / Koordinater 55.75704, 9.41993. Location reference only.

“The palisade”, “The timber buildings” and “The rune-stones and burial mounds”, pp. 6–7. Area of 12.7 ha, oak planks and paired round posts, trench depth 1–1.2 m, traces of three buildings, southeastern wetland wood and estimate 958–985, probably around 968.

16 August 2013, paragraphs on the sampling by Niels Bonde and the Smededammen excavation. Eleven of twelve samples dated; one preserved wood immediately inside the bark. The 1.4 km circuit and most probable date around 968.
Record DO-6476 identifies the pond as Smededammen. Placering / Koordinater 55.75584, 9.42238, approximate orientation at the pond, not the exact sampled plank.

“Danmarks længste bro i tusind år” and “En imponerende konstruktion”. Measurements and construction, wood joints, variable post lengths, suggested traffic, local attribution to Harald and conventional date c. 980.

KUML 52, figs 1 and 3; Danish discussion on pp. 216 and 220–221 and the English conclusion pp. 224–225. The last identified ring yields autumn 979 as a lower limit. Missing bark and revised sapwood statistics give a felling range of roughly 980–1010.
Q996217, coordinate location P625, 55°40′16.4″ N, 9°20′46.9″ E. Approximate site orientation.

Aarbøger for Nordisk Oldkyndighed og Historie 1982 (issued 1984), pp. 111–152. Figure 8 and the English results and conclusion on pp. 145–147: four June/July felling estimates for timbers of the inner ditch barrier; D 701 from the outer bridge, August 980 to May 981; what these can date directly.
Section “Trelleborg”, plan and text. Sixteen houses inside the rampart, cemetery with at least 157 men, women and children, and an alternative association with the village 200 metres away.

Advisory-body evaluation, “Brief description” and statement of Outstanding Universal Value. Danish fortresses with broadly shared geometric layout and four gates, attribution during Harald’s reign and interpretive limits on their purpose.
Geographical data, component 1660-004, Trelleborg in Zealand. Central point 55°23′39″ N, 11°15′55″ E and property maps.

labels.de: Königin Thyra und die Bauleute von Jelling
labels.en: Queen Thyra and the builders of Jelling

summary.de: Gorm lässt seiner Frau Thyra einen Stein setzen. Die Karte markiert den heutigen Standort in Jelling. Der ursprüngliche Aufstellungsort ist ungewiss.
summary.en: Gorm commissions a stone for his wife Thyra. The map shows its present location at Jelling. Its original position is uncertain.

labels.de: um 959 · Ein Silberbecher aus der Grabkammer
labels.en: around 959 · A silver cup from the burial chamber

summary.de: Holz aus der Kammer im Nordhügel ist um 959 datiert. Ein kleiner verzierter Becher und Seidenreste sind erhalten. Wer hier bestattet war, bleibt offen.
summary.en: Wood from the North Mound chamber dates to about 959. A decorated cup and scraps of silk survive. The identity of the person or people buried here is uncertain.

labels.de: um 965 · Haralds Stein und die Hand des Runenmeisters
labels.en: around 965 · Harald’s stone and the carver’s hand

summary.de: Harald gedenkt seiner Eltern und beansprucht die Christianisierung der Dänen für sich. Die Rillen der Schrift legen nahe, dass Ravnunge-Tue die Runen schlug.
summary.en: Harald commemorates his parents and claims credit for the conversion of the Danes. The carved grooves suggest that Ravnunge-Tue cut the inscription.

labels.en: probably around 968 · Oak planks at Smededammen

summary.de: Von zwölf Proben aus der Palisade ließen sich elf datieren. Die Spanne für das Fällen reicht von 958 bis 985, am wahrscheinlichsten ist 968. Der Punkt zeigt den Bereich des heutigen Teichs.
summary.en: Eleven of twelve samples from the palisade could be dated. Felling falls between 958 and 985, most probably around 968. The point marks the area of the present pond.

labels.de: etwa 980–1010 · Eine Holzbrücke über die Talwiesen
labels.en: roughly 980–1010 · A timber bridge across the valley

summary.de: Die Pfosten markieren eine etwa 760 Meter lange Brücke. Der jüngste gemessene Ring stammt von 979. Ohne erhaltene Rinde bleibt der Fällzeitpunkt ungefähr auf 980 bis 1010 eingegrenzt.
summary.en: Timber posts mark a bridge roughly 760 metres long. The latest ring measured dates to 979. With bark missing, felling can be placed only broadly around 980–1010.

labels.en: 980–981 · Two ditches at one building site

summary.de: Hölzer aus der Sperre im inneren Graben und von der Brücke über den äußeren belegen Bauarbeiten 980/81. Der Punkt zeigt die Ringburg bei Slagelse auf Seeland.
summary.en: Timbers from the inner ditch barrier and the bridge over the outer ditch place construction in 980–981. The point marks the ring fortress near Slagelse, Zealand.

summary.de: Wer schlug die Runen zum Gedenken an Thyra? An zwei Steinen lässt sich die Hand eines Handwerkers verfolgen. Kammerhölzer, die Palisade am Dorfteich und zwei große Bauwerke erzählen von der Arbeit für die Könige von Jelling.
summary.en: Who cut the runes in memory of Thyra? The hand of a craftsperson can be traced across two stones. Chamber timbers, the palisade at a village pond and two great building sites reveal work on the scale of the Jelling kings.

labels.de: Sommer 779 · Ein datiertes Holz aus dem Grab von Storhaug
labels.en: summer 779 · A dated timber from the Storhaug burial

summary.de: Die äußerste erhaltene Holzkante datiert das Fällen einer Eiche in den Sommer 779. Das Holz stammt aus dem Grabhügel auf Karmøy. Der Ort dient zum Vergleich mit dem um 820 gebauten Osebergschiff.
summary.en: The outer edge of a piece of oak dates the tree’s felling to summer 779. The timber was found in the mound on Karmøy. The site supplies material for comparison with the Oseberg ship built around 820.

labels.de: 834 · Die Kammer und die Gewebe der beiden Frauen
labels.en: 834 · The chamber and the women’s textiles

summary.de: Das Holz der Kammer datiert die Bestattung in das Jahr 834. Gewebebänder, Seidenstreifen und Werkzeuge erschließen die Arbeit an Textilien, die bereits vor der Bestattung gebraucht wurden.
summary.en: The chamber timbers date the burial to 834. Woven bands, strips of silk and tools provide evidence of textile work and of the use of fabrics before burial.

labels.de: wahrscheinlich 953–975 · Spaten und Tragen im späteren Zugang
labels.en: probably 953–975 · Spades and stretchers in the later passage

summary.de: Werkzeuge datieren den Eingriff am wahrscheinlichsten zwischen 953 und 975. Menschliche Knochen und Teile der Grabausstattung lagen im nachträglich angelegten Gang. Der Anlass bleibt umstritten.
summary.en: Tools place the reopening most probably between 953 and 975. Human bones and parts of the grave furnishings lay in the later access passage. The motive is debated.

labels.de: 1904 · Die Ausgrabung auf Oskar Roms Hof

summary.de: Gustafsons Mannschaft legte das Schiff und die beschädigte Kammer frei. Messzeichnungen und Olaf Værings Aufnahmen halten die Arbeit von 1904 fest.
summary.en: Gustafson’s team exposed the ship and the damaged chamber. Measured drawings and Olaf Væring’s photographs document the excavation of 1904.

summary.de: Gustafson ließ zwei Aquarien für den Osebergsaal des Historischen Museums anfertigen. Darin konnten geschnitzte Tierköpfe unter Wasser gezeigt werden, während ein Verfahren zur Trocknung gesucht wurde.
summary.en: Gustafson commissioned two aquariums for the Oseberg gallery in the Historical Museum. They allowed carved animal heads to be shown underwater while the search for a drying treatment continued.

summary.de: Die Hölzer von Rumpf und Kammer haben ein unterschiedliches Alter. Seidenstreifen, ein im Hügel zurückgelassener Spaten und Aufnahmen von 1904 erzählen, was aus dem Grab zweier Frauen wurde.
summary.en: Hull and chamber have timbers of different ages. Strips of silk, a spade left in the mound and photographs from 1904 trace what happened to the burial of two women.

Chapters X–XI. Witmar as a witness, loss of the books en route, permission to preach, captive Christians, Herigar and his church. The narrative is used for the visit. Modern site identification follows the Swedish History Museum.
Opening paragraphs. Rimbert wrote about 865–875. The museum dates Ansgar and Witmar’s first journey to 830 and distinguishes it from Ansgar’s later visit.
Handelsplatsen Birka. Björkö stood at a Baltic inlet at the time of the trading settlement. The present lake resulted from land uplift. Also explains the deposits called Svarta jorden.
Geographical data, component 555-001, Birka on Björkö (not 555-002, Hovgården). A rounded site point is shared by the harbour, burial and hoard stations.
Collegium Medievale 29, pp. 84–87, “Oseberggravningen”; fig. 2 and pp. 84–85 on five bark-edge samples, the two posts and ridge, the pressure-deformed chamber, and drawings by Glende and Beck.

“What do the motifs on the Oseberg tapestry signify?”, “Exotic goods from Persia and Byzantium” and “The colours that disappeared”; clothing strips, the reversed silk, tools and Sofie Krafft’s 41 drawings of 110 silk pieces.

Opening account of the burial and the four sleighs, followed by “Carvings and ornamentation”. The museum distinguishes three richly carved sleighs and discusses their use before burial.
Hull and rowing holes, the ship built in 820, burial of two women in 834 and the uncertainty over their identities and status.

U841.4 and U842.2, two camps and continued presence; U870.6, four months at Ail Cluaithe; U871.2, Áth Cliath, the leaders, 200 ships and the three groups brought back as captives; U902.2 and U917.4, the defenders driven out and Sitriuc’s entry. U980.1 and U983.2, the battle of Tara and later coalitions.

EMAP Report 7.1, printed pp. 53–55, discussion of captive-taking, trade in enslaved people at Dublin, possibilities of domestic enslavement or onward sale, and the limits of the evidence for different destinations.
Section 2.1.1–2.1.2, printed pp. 3–4. The two placenames, proposed camp by the pool, events of 902 and 917 and changing focus around the Liffey shore at Fishamble Street and Wood Quay.
EMC 1065.0059, obverse and reverse. Entries for ruler, York mint, Raven / Small Cross type, moneyer Æthelferth, spelling on this specimen and weight of 1.17 g.

Rollason, historical sources, the capture in 866–867 and Northumbrian councillors; Blackburn, coinage under Olaf, fig. 82.2 and discussion of the Raven issue under the two Olafs. Craft synthesis, 16–22 Coppergate, pp. 476–481.

“The Jelling Stone”, translated inscription and photographs. The museum dates the raising to c. 965. Harald’s parents and claims about Denmark, Norway and Christianity, earlier Christian objects and Harald Klak’s baptism at Mainz in 826.

Antiquity 97, 1262–1278. Table 1, introduction on the north mound, “Ravnunge-Tue and the Jelling stones”, figures 9–10, “Sources of error” and conclusion. Læborg’s signed dedication and proposed attribution of Jelling 2, weathering at Jelling 1, variants of Thyra’s epithet, and limits of the proposed reburial. The authors give 959/60 for wood from the chamber.

Danish Journal of Archaeology 3(2), pp. 168–170, tables 1–2 and discussion immediately after table 2. Mid-tenth century up to c. 960 for Jelling 1. The chamber wood is reported as 958/59. Historical dating proposals for Jelling 2 differ.

Figures 2–6 and English summary under “Stone for his parents” and “Small silver cup”. Vertical and horizontal writing, reliefs, purple silk, and the 4.3 cm silver cup with gilding and entwined animals from the north mound.

Nature 601, pp. 388–391. Three worked pieces of wood, the metal-tool cuts and Norse depositional context, Table 1 and Fig. 2 on the radiocarbon signal and counting rings to the surviving outside edge. Published online in 2021.

“Discovery of the Site and Initial Excavations (1960–1968)”. Turf construction in eight buildings, bronze ring-headed pin in a cooking pit, stone lamp and spindle whorl in another building, ship nails and iron slag.
Collection entry “Bog Iron Nail, L’Anse aux Meadows, Newfoundland”. Slag and iron from the excavated nail support smelting of local bog ore. The four nails illustrated on that page are reproductions.
Appendix 1, pp. 30–31, manuscript witnesses AM 544 4to and GKS 1005 fol., and “B. Differences”: one planned expedition in Eiríks saga rauða and four in Grœnlendinga saga.

Introductory chronology, “Geographical areas of the Norse settlements and settlement pattern” and “Natural resources”. The written sources place one migration from Iceland to Southwest Greenland under Erik the Red around 985. The Western Settlement was in the Nuuk region; archaeological and radiocarbon evidence in the Eastern Settlement reaches at least the mid-fifteenth century.

Printed pp. 183–186, keelson sample D2-4 and its final spring ring; pp. 187–189, “Parallels in Irish and English ship-finds”, esp. fig. 55 (Fishamble Street stems T357/T364 and corresponding elements of Skuldelev 2) and text on parallels in Danish-built vessels.
Opening account, dating the build to around 1042 in the vicinity of Dublin through the oak tree rings.

Collection overview, paragraphs on wooden pathways and property boundaries, reused ship timbers in dock walls, drains and paths; the Fishamble Street amber worker’s floor with several hundred flakes and splinters.

Printed pp. 146, 148–149 and 152–153. P. 146 describes the transmitted attestations of 1409, 1414 and 1424. Document 49 gives the three Sunday banns, local and foreign witnesses, and the two clerics’ seals. Document 52 names the four men who attended in 1408 and attested in Iceland in 1414. Facsimile of the edition with facing original text and Danish translation.

“Kirkens vinduer” on the round arched east window and other flat lintels; “Brylluppet i Hvalseyfjordens kirke” on the September 1408 wedding, the document at Garðar in 1409 and the journey back to Iceland.
Collection item DMR-217737, ruin 1, group Ø83, NKAH 4427 (Hvalsey church). Location field 60.82883° N, 45.78261° W. Modern survey photograph dated 1935.

Section “Segmented metal foil beads”, pp. 161 and 165 and fig. 5a–c (e.g. ASR9x113 59). Manufacture, silver foil, amber-brown and colourless outer glass, joined segments and the visible structure of broken specimens. Opening section on the continued small-scale production in the ninth century.
Object 106842_HST, accession 34000, Bj 515. Find context, excavator, 1877, silver and glass. The 2021 exhibition label gives the proposed reading of the Arabic inscription.

Scanning 37, pp. 131–137. Materials, p. 132 and supplementary fig. S1, for burial layout, oval brooches, clothes, position and approximate date. Results and figs. 1–3 for filing marks and composition. Discussion accompanying fig. 4 for the favoured dedication and the conditional reading “God willing” if a missing stroke is supplied.
Media ID ba934209-835b-4b3c-ab7a-73126a4375a9, direct association with object 106842_HST, named photographer and CC BY 4.0 licence.
The Archaeology of York 17/5, table 11 and pp. 341–345, figs 140–142. Context, needle binding, shaping the heel, worn sole and outline of a probable patch.
SC1981-7_SF13517, catalogue 1309; coverage c. 930–975, madder at the ankle and no dye elsewhere.
The Archaeology of York 17/11, pp. 1787–1788, 1800–1803 and figs 843–844. A 4B pit, dyes and needles, including their concentration on Tenement C and a previously unused silk offcut.

The Archaeology of York 8/5. Abstract and Period 4B on the properties; Structure 5/1, pp. 622–624 and fig. 212; provisional building chronology p. 798. The report dates wall timbers to winter 961/62 and identifies reused wood at the entrance.
Monument MYO5075, Location: British National Grid SE 6044 5169. Converted to WGS84 and rounded for orientation.

“Gorm the Old authored Denmark’s name certificate” and “Two monuments from Danish history”. Gorm’s commissioning formula, the museum’s rendering of Thyra’s epithet, c. 950, and the photograph “The small Jelling stone” by Roberto Fortuna, CC BY-SA 2.0.

Abstract of chapter 12 in Jelling – Monuments and Landscape, pp. 313–332. The smaller stone is no longer in its original position. Excavation during protection works in 2011 re-examined the central area and the position of the larger stone.

SC1365, “Summary” and “Location”; twin summits, 1974–75 excavation, fifth trench on the eastern side, bedding trench, vitrified stone and three radiocarbon determinations in the sixth to ninth centuries. Site coordinates WGS84, 55.936756 N, 4.563298 W.
“Under siege”, identification of the 870 siege of the Rock, the Dublin leaders Olaf and Ivar, and forced removals following the four-month siege.

Chapter 7, pp. 102–108, Figs. 7.2–4 and Table 7.1. Hearth 4A76P west of the brook, 15 grey-green chert flakes one metre west of the fire, the nail one metre southeast. With 1950 as BP reference, the reported two-sigma charcoal ranges are AD 900–910 and 960–1040 for Beta-252632 and AD 990–1150 for Beta-252633. The map uses their outer envelope; occupation was episodic. pp. 115–116 and Tables 7.5–6 describe birds on the other, upper terrace.

Arctic Anthropology 49(1), pp. 68–87, DOI 10.1353/arc.2012.0015. Abstract and Table 1 discuss the site in relation to Beothuk ancestors, the charcoal determinations for hearth 4A76P2 and seasonal harvesting of birds.
First two paragraphs. Archaeological evidence of Indigenous use over six millennia and Dorset camps on the south shore more than two centuries before the Norse.

summary.en: Rimbert recounts the monks’ arrival and describes captives and the town’s reeve, Hergeir. The point marks the trading settlement on Björkö.

summary.en: The annals say that Amlaíb and Ímar brought captives to Áth Cliath. They count ships and name groups of people who were taken. Individual fates go unrecorded.

summary.de: Unter Amlaíb mac Gofraid begann in York die Prägung der Rabenpennys. Einzelne Stücke könnten noch unter seinem Nachfolger entstanden sein. Die Karte zeigt die Münzstadt.
summary.en: York began issuing Raven pennies under Amlaíb mac Gofraid. Some specimens may belong to his successor. The map identifies the mint town.

summary.de: Die drei Hölzer datieren Arbeiten auf 1021. Nägel, Schlacke und Spinnwirtel bezeugen weitere Tätigkeiten im Lager, deren genaues Jahr offenbleibt.
summary.en: Three timbers date work at the camp to 1021. Nails, slag and a spindle whorl attest other activities there whose precise year is unknown.

labels.de: 1042 · Die Eiche für die Maststütze von Skuldelev 2
labels.en: 1042 · The oak for the keelson of Skuldelev 2

summary.de: Die Eiche für die Maststütze fiel im Mai oder Juni 1042. Der Bau des Langschiffs wird im Raum Dublin vermutet. Zwei in der Stadt ausgegrabene Stevenstücke zeigen vergleichbare Arbeit an anderen Schiffen.
summary.en: The oak for the keelson was felled in May or June 1042. The longship was probably built in the Dublin region. Two stem timbers excavated in the town show comparable work on other vessels.

labels.de: 1408 · Die Hochzeit von Sigríður und Þorsteinn

summary.de: Im September 1408 heirateten Sigríður Björnsdóttir und Þorsteinn Ólafsson in der Kirche von Hvalsey. Die Bestätigung der Geistlichen in Garðar und spätere Zeugenaussagen in Island betreffen dieselbe Ehe.
summary.en: In September 1408 Sigríður Björnsdóttir and Þorsteinn Ólafsson married in Hvalsey church. The Garðar clerics’ declaration and later testimony in Iceland concern the same marriage.

summary.de: Neun Stationen führen vom Markt am Fluss in Ribe über Gefangene in Dublin, eine Königsmünze und einen Runenstein bis zur nordischen Siedlung auf Neufundland. Ein Ausblick führt ins mittelalterliche Grönland.
summary.en: Nine stops lead from the riverside market in Ribe to captives in Dublin, a royal penny, a rune stone and Norse woodworking in Newfoundland. A final stop visits medieval Greenland.
